assets.title: Byzantine archery range
changes: Compiled a static self-contained GLB with embedded WebP textures, KHR_mesh_quantization and KHR_texture_transform; no Draco, Meshopt or KTX decoder is required.
Converted original source materials to roughness/metalness PBR, preserving authored UV coordinates and supplied surface normal maps. Texture resolution is capped at 1024 pixels.
Centered the complete geometry footprint and grounded its visible foundation. Sub-millimetre quantization tolerance is corrected by runtime precise vertex bounds.
Assembled the original stone/brick teaching tower, tiled arcade, bow racks, circular practice targets, canvas shelter and three authored bows using the source actor socket transforms.
Removed separate ground decals, particle/death variants and hidden below-ground foundation skirts. Clipped source triangles at source Y=0 while interpolating normals and UV sets.
Kept the static bow rack geometry; the source weapon attack animation is not included.
Normalized uniformly to the 9.3 metre usable inner plot. No axis was scaled independently.

validation.warningExplanation: Tangent-space normals are generated by the renderer from the supplied normals and UVs, which is supported by the game's fixed Three.js r170 renderer. The validator cautions about portability to unrelated renderers.

assets.title: Stonecutters quarry
changes: Compiled a static self-contained GLB with embedded WebP textures, KHR_mesh_quantization and KHR_texture_transform; no Draco, Meshopt or KTX decoder is required.
Converted original source materials to roughness/metalness PBR, preserving authored UV coordinates and supplied surface normal maps. Texture resolution is capped at 1024 pixels.
Centered the complete geometry footprint and grounded its visible foundation. Sub-millimetre quantization tolerance is corrected by runtime precise vertex bounds.

Welded coincident photogrammetry vertices while preserving per-loop UVs, then derived a 7934-triangle rock LOD and 238-triangle small-debris LOD from Boulder 01. Repeated pieces use different scale and rotation.
Preserved Daniel Andersson's authored wheelbarrow and ladder geometry and UVs, converted their legacy material to PBR, and repositioned them within a custom medieval workyard.
Added original bevelled oak frames, forged joint straps and nails, hand-operated windlass, wound and hanging hemp rope, mason bench, pickaxe and mallet. All supplied geometry is static.
Retained the original rope fiber and mineral rock photographic detail through PBR material conversion.
Used an irregular shallow earth apron with perimeter at ground level. No terrain excavation, external geometry or negative-height dependency is required.
Normalized uniformly to a 9.15 metre source envelope. The renderer fits that envelope to the 9.3 metre usable plot.

Composed a stepped rock face, rough hewn benches, dressed-stone stockpile, open timber workshop and hand derrick with a stone in the lifting sling. Workshop front clear headroom is approximately 2.1 metres after runtime fit.

validation.warningExplanation: Tangent-space normals are generated by the renderer from the supplied normals and UVs, which is supported by the game's fixed Three.js r170 renderer. The validator cautions about portability to unrelated renderers.

assets.title: Timber-shored iron mine
changes: Compiled a static self-contained GLB with embedded WebP textures, KHR_mesh_quantization and KHR_texture_transform; no Draco, Meshopt or KTX decoder is required.
Converted original source materials to roughness/metalness PBR, preserving authored UV coordinates and supplied surface normal maps. Texture resolution is capped at 1024 pixels.
Centered the complete geometry footprint and grounded its visible foundation. Sub-millimetre quantization tolerance is corrected by runtime precise vertex bounds.

Welded coincident photogrammetry vertices while preserving per-loop UVs, then derived a 7934-triangle rock LOD and 238-triangle small-debris LOD from Boulder 01. Repeated pieces use different scale and rotation.
Preserved Daniel Andersson's authored wheelbarrow and ladder geometry and UVs, converted their legacy material to PBR, and repositioned them within a custom medieval workyard.
Added original bevelled oak frames, forged joint straps and nails, hand-operated windlass, wound and hanging hemp rope, mason bench, pickaxe and mallet. All supplied geometry is static.
Retained the original rope fiber and mineral rock photographic detail through PBR material conversion.
Used an irregular shallow earth apron with perimeter at ground level. No terrain excavation, external geometry or negative-height dependency is required.
Normalized uniformly to a 9.15 metre source envelope. The renderer fits that envelope to the 9.3 metre usable plot.

Composed three rock masses around a genuine recessed gallery with three braced timber support frames, roof and side shoring, plank handbarrow ramp, ore sorting crib and manual hauling windlass. There are no rails or powered machinery. Central portal clear span after runtime fit is approximately 2.27 metres wide by 2.5 metres high.

renderValidation.method: CPU Cycles renders of the exact published optimized GLBs, at the runtime uniform placement scale. The preview-only visible worker is 1.8 metres tall and is not included in any facility GLB.
renderValidation.webglRuntimeLoader: The actual locally vendored Three.js r170 GLTFLoader decoded every embedded texture and checked finite visible geometry, exact bounds and required extensions.
renderValidation.limitation: This checks asset decoding and geometry. It is not a live physical GPU frame-rate measurement.
